findings.description: Tearing the worktree down before publishing the park makes a teardown failure discard a completed review. Concrete path: `removeWorktree` returns an error (`git worktree prune` failing, or `Unseal`/`RemoveAll` failing on a file the reviewer's tool server left behind) and `Supervise` returns before `supervision.park`. `run.json` is then still `reviewing` with `Reviewer` set to the now-dead supervisor pid, while `findings.json` is on disk. `awaitVerdict` (cmd/scrat/review.go:95) only returns on a terminal state or `awaiting-response`, so `scrat review --wait` and `scrat continue --wait` poll forever with no deadline, and `parked` (internal/reviewer/respond.go:76) refuses both `scrat respond` and `scrat continue` because the state is not `awaiting-response`. The only exit is `scrat cancel`. Before the reorder, the run parked and the teardown error was returned afterwards, so the review was still usable. The ordering the change wants is compatible with still parking on a teardown error (attempt the removal, then park regardless and join the error), but which verdict a run gets when its worktree cannot be removed is a decision for a person.

The retrospective records a fix that this commit did not make. Line 29 states the rule as "`ask-user` escalates, nothing blocking is clean, the cap escalates, otherwise park" - four clauses - and line 30 states "`After` no longer looks at patchability at all, so whether a document holds the change has one owner again". The shipped `dialogue.After` (internal/dialogue/dialogue.go:19) has five clauses and does look at patchability: `len(Answerable(classified)) == 0` reads `classified.Patchable`. The specification this change writes (specs/review-dialogue/spec.md:9) states the five-clause rule. So the one document that explains why the rule is what it is describes a different rule from the one in the code and the spec, and it is the document a later reader will trust about the reasoning.

"`scrat continue` refuses while any blocking finding has no response" is no longer what the code does, and the stated intent for this change includes making the design state the same rule as the specification. `Unanswered` (internal/dialogue/responses.go:78) now waits only on findings that block *and* are patchable, and the specification was updated to match (specs/review-dialogue/spec.md:143). Reachable counterexample: a round returning `[{error, auto-fix f1}, {error, no-op f2}]` has `Answerable == [f1]`, so it parks; answering f1 alone lets `scrat continue` proceed with f2 - a blocking finding - unanswered. The design sentence says that is refused.

`everythingIsAnswered` tells the author "every blocking finding of this round now has a response", and after the change to `Unanswered` that can be false. Same reachable input as f3: a parked round holding `[{error, auto-fix f1}, {error, no-op f2}]` waits only on f1, so `scrat respond --finding f1 --fixed` prints this line (cmd/scrat/respond.go:71) while f2 blocks and has no response. The message is the author's only signal that the round is fully answered, so it asserts something the change deliberately stopped being true.

The concurrency test can pass while proving nothing. `recorded[position]` is only set true when `RecordResponse` returned no error, and the assertion loop skips every position that failed, so a run in which all eight recordings error is a pass. Nothing asserts that any response was recorded at all, and nothing asserts the stored count. It also exercises eight goroutines inside one process, while the requirement it covers (specs/review-dialogue/spec.md:127) is about two `scrat respond` invocations; the file-level mechanism is the same, so this is a reasonable proxy, but the vacuous-pass hole is worth closing with a check that at least the expected responses are present.

`RecordResponse` reads the whole document before appending, and uses that pre-append snapshot for the caller's `Unanswered` report (internal/reviewer/respond.go:43). Under the concurrency this change exists to support, two `scrat respond` processes each compute the still-unanswered list from a snapshot that cannot see the other's line, so the printed "%d findings still have none" can name findings that were just answered. The error direction is safe - a process can only over-report what is unanswered, never under-report - and `scrat continue` re-reads from disk, so no round advances wrongly. Separately, the read can fail on a line another process is mid-append, and because the read precedes the append the author's claim is then not recorded at all and the command refuses with a parsing error, where a retry would succeed.

`SaveResponses` remains an exported whole-document rewrite of an artifact the new requirement declares append-only (specs/review-dialogue/spec.md:127). Its only remaining caller is internal/report/parked_test.go:128, so no production path violates the invariant today, but the type now offers two writers of `responses.jsonl` with opposite guarantees and nothing stops the next caller picking the rewriting one.

The exhaustive test's new oracle repeats the pattern the retrospective names as the reason the original defect survived a green suite. `answerable(held)` here is a line-for-line restatement of `dialogue.Answerable` (internal/dialogue/dialogue.go:25) - blocks and effective action is auto-fix - so the 512-subset sweep confirms the sentence was implemented rather than that the outcome is right, exactly as retrospective.md:33-34 describes of the previous oracle. Worth knowing when reading this test as evidence.

risk_rationale: The routing and append-only changes are bounded and covered by tests that would fail before the fix, but the park/teardown reorder adds a path that leaves a finished review unreachable and hangs `--wait`, and three documents the change touches now state a rule the code does not implement.
